p: What was said in the name of
זֵכֶר צַדִּיקִים וּקְדוֹשִׁים לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the righteous and holy be for a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
that the meal of a Pidyon HaBen
which serve to rectify the blemish of the bris,
שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה וְכוּלֵּי
of Yaakov Avinu in which he did not see, etc.
and he said, "My strength and the first of my vigor."
that the complete rectification in this
יִהְיֶה בְּעֵת שֶׁיִּתְבַּטֵּל הַמִּיתָה מִן הָעוֹלָם
will come when death is abolished from the world,
which came about through the first blemish.
one who refines himself in this to the utmost
and Eliyahu, the angel of the bris,
And Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was placed in the world for the ultimate purpose of this rectification
מֵהַמֵּאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנִים שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
from the hundred and thirty years of Adam HaRishon
and about him our Sages of blessed memory said
And regarding this it is said of him,
"My strength and the first of my vigor,"
for he refined himself so thoroughly
that he was devoid of this desire,
like Adam HaRishon before the sin,
of whom it is said, "And they were not ashamed."
what even the lowest of the low would not say,
"He said so in order to bring forth offspring";
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוּם הֶרְגֵּשׁ בּוּשָׁה
for he had no sense of shame at all
just as it will be in the future,
when the rectification will be complete:
"And I will give you a heart of flesh,"
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קלז, ב)
and it is stated in the holy Zohar (I 137b):
And the particular nature of the rectification here
is that he is rectified at the root,
and then deliberate sins become for him like merits.
And this is specifically with Yisrael:
because they are bound to the root
and to the source of holiness, beyond intellect,
to turn the deliberate sins into merits.
This is not so with the nations of the world;
teshuvah of this kind does not avail them,
רַק שֶׁדָּנִים אוֹתָם בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא שָׁם
rather they are judged "as he is there."
are the Ten Utterances of the work of Creation
and the Ten Commandments at Matan Torah.
where it says, "And Elokim said, Let there be light,"
as it says, "And wisdom, from nothingness it is found."
And Bereishis is the beginning of the source,
And corresponding to this is also
the first utterance of the Ten Commandments,
of why it is not stated in the language of a command.
It is because it is a matter of faith in the root,
לָכֵן אֵין שַׁיָּיכוּת בָּזֶה שׁוּם צִיוּוּי
therefore no command whatsoever applies to it,
אִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִין לֹא יוֹעִיל הַצִּיוּוּי
if he does not believe, the command will not help.
Rather, to the souls of Yisrael
לִהְיוֹת דְּבוּקִים בְּהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמַעְלָה מִן הַדַּעַת
so that they cleave to the root beyond intellect.
And also the ten plagues in Mitzrayim,
שֶׁהָיוּ גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת
which likewise corresponded to the ten holy sefiros,
striking for Mitzrayim and healing for Yisrael.
the refinement was in the attribute of Chochmah,
וּלְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבוֹתָם
"But for all Bnei Yisrael there was light in their dwellings."
And in the plague of the firstborn
came the culmination of the refinement of Yisrael's holiness,
for they cleave to the root of the Ayin
and become "My son, My firstborn, Yisrael,"
which is the beginning of thought at the root;
and the firstborn of the opposite side
the firstborn of Yisrael were then sanctified for their redemption.
Now, the matter of Pesach Sheni,
for one who was tamei or who was on a distant road,
הוּא מְרַמֵּז עַל תְּשׁוּבָה וְתִיקּוּן בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ
alludes to teshuvah and rectification at the root,
whereby deliberate sins become like merits,
as is written in the holy Zohar
And this is an even greater distance
than one who is tamei through a corpse,
as is written (in the holy Zohar there):
And the principal tumah that is deferred to Pesach Sheni
which is unlike other tumos that issue from one's own body,
שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי קִלְקוּל בְּחֵטְא פְּרָטִי
which come through a corruption in a particular sin,
which comes for the sin of lashon hara
עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁמְּטַמֵּא עַצְמוֹ לְמֵת מִצְוָה
through one's defiling himself for a mes mitzvah,
as they said (in the Gemara, Sukkah 25a)
were the bearers of Yosef's coffin,
who became tamei through Nadav and Avihu.
at the season of Pesach from corpse-tumah,
זוּלַת בְּעֵת הַהֶכְרֵחַ עַל יְדֵי מִצְוָה
except when compelled by a mitzvah;
וְכֵן בְּוַדַּאי לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם יִשְׂרָאֵל
would set out on a distant road
unless compelled for the sake of a great mitzvah.
וְעִם כָּל זֶה נִרְמָז מִזֶּה בִּפְנִימִיּוּת
Nevertheless, there is alluded in this, inwardly,
as is known from the holy Zohar cited above.
That is, the matter of corpse-tumah
is known to stem from the first blemish,
which brought death into the world;
and also the matter of a distant road,
שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּל מִצְוַת הַפֶּסַח
which entails the neglect of the mitzvah of Pesach,
שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ וְכַדּוֹמֶה
brought about by pikuach nefesh and the like,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִסִּיבַּת פְּגַם הָרִאשׁוֹן
is likewise a result of the first blemish.
And even when one forgoes some mitzvah
for the sake of another mitzvah,
עַל כָּל פָּנִים נֶעְדָּר הָאוֹר מִצְוָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
the light of the first mitzvah is in any case missing,
as is known from the holy Zohar,
that he sensed by the scent of their garments
that they had not recited Krias Shema in its time,
although they had been occupied with another mitzvah
that one is kept from a mitzvah on account of a mitzvah.
when such a thing befell them,
their hearts were greatly embittered within them:
why had such a thing happened to them,
to be pushed away from the collective holiness of Yisrael?
Although it was not out of disdain,
"Why should we be held back from offering," etc.
וּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And in truth, even from Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
the substance of the matter was hidden,
and he said to them, "Stand, and I will hear," etc.,
for according to the strict line of the law
there was no remedy for this,
since once its day has passed, its offering is void.
But they brought about a remedy for this
through the breaking of their hearts:
the drawing forth of the Torah's parashah of Pesach Sheni.
This is the aspect of "naaseh v'nishma,"
in which they bring about new Torah;
and merit is brought about through one who is meritorious,
and therefore it came about that there was said through them
וּלְרַמֵּז זֶה אָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
"An individual is deferred, but a community is not deferred";
for the entire holiness of Pesach Sheni
who are distant in their souls
from the collective holiness of Yisrael,
they are rectified at the root,
so that deliberate sins become like merits.
Now, it is stated in the holy Zohar (there)
that the holiness of the first Pesach
and Pesach Sheni descends from above to below,
For the essential holiness of Pesach Mitzrayim
comes only through an arousal from Above,
for holiness shone upon them in full measure
to bring them out of the utmost distance
to the very root of holiness,
And this is the aspect of "with Me is the crushed"
meaning that Hashem Yisbarach then draws
the souls of Yisrael close to holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וָאֶשָּׂא אֶתְכֶם עַל כַּנְפֵי נְשָׁרִים
as it says, "And I carried you on the wings of eagles
and this is the meaning of ascending from below to above.
הִיא דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
comes specifically through an arousal from below:
that he has become very distant from the collective holiness of Yisrael,
and his heart is broken within him,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְתַכְלִית הַתִּיקּוּן
and through this he merits the ultimate rectification,
that everything be rectified at the root.
וְהוּא עִנְיַן אֲנִי אֶת דַּכָּא אֶשְׁכּוֹן
This is the meaning of "I dwell with the crushed"
that, as it were, He lowers His holiness
from the first Pesach until Pesach Sheni
belong to the holiness of Pesach
(as is stated in the holy Zohar there):
our forefathers were nourished from the flat cake
that they had taken out of Mitzrayim
and they ate from the dough
the taste of the holiness of the mitzvah from the first Exodus,
when Hashem Yisbarach shone upon them
with the radiance of His Shechinah from Above,
so that the dough was not able
This is the aspect of the nullification of the yetzer hara
which is the leaven in the dough
and on the fifteenth of Iyar they were given
which is a matter of preparation for receiving the Torah
that he exert himself to sanctify and purify himself
even in a state of distance
owing to the yetzer hara in his soul.
the counting of the seven weeks,
that on Pesach Sheni begins the sefirah of Hod,
And it is known that Moshe is the groomsman of the King
and Aharon the attendant of the Queen;
and the role of the King's groomsman
is the drawing down of holiness from Above,
from the aspect of arousal from Above,
is purification in holiness from the side of the recipient.
from the side of arousal from Above,
which is the holiness of the first Pesach;
which is man's sanctifying himself from his own side
and this is the role of the Queen's attendant.
And this month is called Chodesh Ziv,
which is the radiance and splendor
alluding to the rectification of the blemish of the bris,
וְכָל עִנְיַן יוֹפִי וְזִיו קְלַסְתֵּר פָּנִים
And every mention of beauty and radiance of countenance
refers to the holiness of the bris,
as they said of Rabbi Yochanan
that he was one of the beautiful men of Yerushalayim
"I come from the seed of Yosef"
וְהַחוֹדֶשׁ אִייָר הוּא נֶגֶד מִדַּת יְסוֹד
And the month of Iyar corresponds to the attribute of Yesod;
therefore it is called by the name Ziv,
as is explained in the holy Zohar
And the culmination of the rectification is completed in Chodesh Ziv.
And we have stated an allusion to this in the Midrash
"Why was the Torah not given immediately
A parable to a king whose son fell ill," etc.;
אָמַר לָהֶם עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא בְּנִי לְזִיווֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"he said to them, My son has not yet regained his radiance," etc.
(as explained in Rosh Chodesh Iyar, maamar 1).
And in Chodesh Ziv the healing is completed
along with the full rectification of the soul,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשִׂים מוּכָנִים לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה
and through this they become prepared to receive the Torah.
